summary: The refusal at segment 0 step 55 is an unsupported JavaScript placeholder, not a C precondition. C accepts the adjacent square containing a visible ordinary monster far enough to report that the monster would not appreciate lock picking, then returns PICKLOCK_LEARNED_SOMETHING so the apply command spends a turn. JavaScript currently throws for any monster at the chosen square before checking visibility or map disguise, so it both rejects valid C behavior and skips the recorded message and turn. Port the whole partially implemented lock.c:pick_lock function, including its other fail-closed branches, while preserving its existing doapply, do_loot_cont, and doopen_indir callers.

source.branch: In the adjacent-door arm, C first gets mtmp with m_at(cc.x, cc.y). A visible monster whose M_AP_TYPE is neither M_AP_FURNITURE nor M_AP_OBJECT enters the monster response arm. For this skeleton-key case C prints "I don't think the giant ant would appreciate that." with mon_nam() and returns PICKLOCK_LEARNED_SOMETHING. A credit card used on a shopkeeper or the Oracle has its own verbalize branch. A door-mimicking monster is handled next; otherwise even a monster can fall through to ordinary door/map checks. The mere presence of a monster is not a precondition.
callers: apply.c:doapply() calls pick_lock(obj, 0, 0, NULL) for LOCK_PICK, CREDIT_CARD, and SKELETON_KEY (4285-4289); the recorded direct apply path reaches this caller. JavaScript is already wired through apply.js:doapply().
pickup.c:do_loot_cont() calls pick_lock(unlocktool, ox, oy, cobj) for container autounlock (2125-2135); JavaScript is already wired through pickup.js:do_loot_cont().
lock.c:doopen_indir() calls pick_lock(unlocktool, cc.x, cc.y, NULL) for door autounlock (876-883); JavaScript is already wired through lock.js:doopen_indir().
dependencies: For the reproduced ordinary visible-monster arm, reuse the existing source-backed m_at (monst.js), canseemon (display.js), M_AP_TYPE (const.js), mon_nam (do_name.js), and ttyPline (tty_message.js). Apply.c converts every nonzero PICKLOCK result, including PICKLOCK_LEARNED_SOMETHING, to ECMD_TIME.

The whole pick_lock function also has a distinct CREDIT_CARD shopkeeper/Oracle arm requiring SetVoice and verbalize, and a door-mimic arm requiring is_door_mappear and stumble_onto_mimic. C then calls maybe_absorb_item(mtmp, pick, 50, 10), whose result it discards; if still unported, preserve the gap with note_unported('lock.c maybe_absorb_item') rather than inventing effects.

Audit the existing AUTOUNLOCK_UNTRAP and autounlock artifact-touch branches against lock.c:472-480, 605-612, and 628-630. could_untrap and touch_artifact return values control C behavior; untrap results are discarded. The corresponding JavaScript paths currently include fail-closed throws in pick_lock.

evidence: The saved baseline challenges/evaluations/20261007095608-v26.json at evaluation commit 2b9e0c1d8384b8ca8ab5c19dc12a426f3ac42e44 records 55/63 matching screens and cursors, 2711/2719 matching RNG calls, and 8 remaining screens. The exact queue first stop is segment 0, zero-based step 55: UnsupportedLockError from the monster-on-square placeholder.

The independently recorded C input challenges/cases/v26/v26-lock-key-visible-monster.session.json has key h at segment 0 step 55 and shows the message "I don't think the giant ant would appreciate that." The step advances the turn; its RNG trace includes mcalcmove, maybe_generate_rnd_mon, gethungry, and moveloop_core.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/lock.c:559-570 checks m_at, canseemon, and disguise type before emitting the ordinary-monster response and returning PICKLOCK_LEARNED_SOMETHING. Lines 571-576 separately handle a door mimic. This directly contradicts treating m_at() != NULL as a lock-picking precondition.

The JavaScript placeholder is js/lock.js:867-870: it throws UnsupportedLockError whenever m_at returns a monster. Its message template at js/lock.js:148 says "picking a lock requires ..."; this is internal fail-closed diagnostic wording, not a C game message or behavior.

Because pick_lock is an existing partial implementation and the unported arm is inside that whole C function, selection.md requires a file-port of lock.c:pick_lock, not a narrow divergence-fix. The source already has production callers in apply.c, pickup.c, and lock.c, with corresponding JavaScript calls in apply.js, pickup.js, and lock.js; validate their wiring while implementing the whole function.
